correctness.rationale: Smoothness bDelta!=0 follows from separability of x*g(x^3), with a cubic discriminant. The 4x4 Cartier coefficient matrix is exactly reconstructed by multinomial expansion; its determinant is 3b^2 u v^2. Restriction to v=0 proves u nonzero on every smooth member, so Cartier a-number is 0,1,2 only. For the rank-one B block, Cartier iteration uses M^(7)M, and the scalar w^(7) z factors as 3(a+1)^2 R(a). The degree-five R is separable and avoids a=0,-1,-2, giving exactly five geometric rank-zero Pryms. The quotient elliptic factor is ordinary on v=0 and rank additivity holds under the prime-to-seven isogeny. Scheme minors generate (v), while determinant has v^2. Both included verification programs were executed successfully, including complete F7 checks; finite samples are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The exact five-point rank-zero Prym locus and absence of Prym rank two describe the arithmetic geometry of the entire smooth two-parameter family studied for C6-symmetric superspecial genus-four curves, in the first p≡1 mod3 case. The difference between a reduced Cartier-rank-two locus and a doubled Hasse divisor is a structural phenomenon. This closes a natural coefficient-level stratification gap left by the motivating paper, not an arbitrary isolated small computation or a numerical increment to a known count. No universal downstream application is claimed.
